name: Violet-Slate
lede: Violet-Slate is a cool, blue-grey slate with only a faint purple cast, plated by Ridgway in 1912 and still filed by ISCC-NBS in 1955 as a plain grayish blue.

sections.title: A slate with a violet whisper
sections.body:
Ridgway recorded this hue twice in 1912, at plate XLIX, hue 53'''', tone i, and again at plate LII, hue 59''''', tone i, and the ISCC-NBS system later filed it as block 186, a grayish blue [1]. The "violet" in the name is a modest one: measured in LCH it comes out at lightness 43, chroma only 5 and hue 250 degrees, so the color reads first as grey and only faintly as cool blue-violet [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[slate-grey]], [[dark-plumbeous]] and [[basalt-grey]], at 3.6, 3.6 and 3.8 ΔE [1]. Its nearest distinct neighbors are [[slate-grey]] and [[dark-plumbeous]], both almost the same at a distance of 3.6 [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this grey-blue in 474 of 23,781 paintings (1.99%, as photographed), more common than 68% of the named colors we track [3]. It most often plays a mid-tone, in 34% of its 177 strongest matches [3]. Claude Monet is its most devoted painter, at 5.4 times the baseline rate across his 50 works here, and it shares canvases with Squirrel Grey far more than chance [3]. The earliest dated match runs to 1100, eight centuries before Ridgway's own 1912 record; the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof the pigment was there, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
